title: Top level configuration
description:
The top level configuration consists of 3 required elements:

 - simulation
 - write_results
 - components

and optional elements:

 - external_libs
 - friction_correlations
 - nusselt_correlations
 - materials

Description of each element is provided below.

FrictionRS.title: Friction within Riemann solver + junctions
FrictionRS.description:
Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``yes``
       
- ``yes``: Simulation will consider friction within Riemann solver - useful in case
  of high dP + coarse mesh

- ``no``: No correction within the Riemann solver - Friction still active but potentially
  less accurate in case of high dP + coarse mesh

R_correction.title: Mechanical equilibrium correction - Introduction of an extra fluid equation
R_correction.description:
Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``yes``

- ``yes``: Mechanical equilibrium correction is activated - Useful in case
  of density discontinuity + coarse mesh close to the critical region

- ``no``: No mechanical equilibrium correction - Less accurate in case of density 
  discontinuity + coarse mesh close to the critical region - More accurate  
  and robust far from critical region

explicit_tolerance.title: Criteria for switching from explicit to implicit
explicit_tolerance.description:
Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``9e-4``

Reducing this value leads to prioritizing the explicit scheme over the implicit scheme.
We therefore expect further flow stabilization before the implicit scheme is activated.

implicit_tolerance.title: Tolerance of implicit solver
implicit_tolerance.description:
Reducing this value leads to longer computation times due to the use of smaller time
steps, but potentially increased robustness.

step_controller_gain.title: Gain of PI controller
step_controller_gain.description:
Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``4.0``

This value is related to automatic time step management - It is advised to modify
implicit_tolerance and keep the default value of the gain.

max_time_step.title: Maximum time step (s)
max_time_step.description: Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``50.0``

active.title: Writing results to hdf5 files activation
active.description: Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``true``

file.title: File name to store output data

minimum_time.title: Minimum space between saved points (s)
minimum_time.description: Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``0.0``

active2D.title: Writing to results to hdf5 files  - Mesh2D components
active2D.description: Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``true``

time_between_2D_writes.title: Time interval between two consecutive 2D result writes (s)
time_between_2D_writes.description: Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``3600.0``

external_libs.title: External dynamic libraries
external_libs.description:
Optional list of dynamic libraries (DLL) to load at startup.
Each entry is the library name without the ``.dll`` extension.

.. code:: yaml

  external_libs:
  - name_of_my_dll_1
  - name_of_my_dll_2

friction_correlations.title: Fanning friction factor correlations

friction.title: Correlation name
friction.description:
Unique name used to reference this correlation in the ``friction`` field
of channel components.

base.title: Built-in correlation to use as base
base.description:
Required only for Case 2: built-in correlation with custom parameters.
Identifies which built-in initialization to use for this entry.

Re_min.title: Minimum Reynolds number for Katheder activation (katheder only, default 1000)
Re_min.description:
Reynolds number threshold below which the Katheder correlation returns zero
and only laminar friction applies (default: 1000). Set to 0 to activate
Katheder for all Re > 0.

friction_correlations.description:
Optional list of named friction correlations available to channel components.
Three use cases are supported: built-in with defaults, built-in with custom
parameters, or user-defined via external DLL.
See :ref:`friction-correlations-details` for details and examples.

nusselt_correlations.title: Nusselt number correlations

nusselt.title: Correlation name
nusselt.description:
Unique name used to reference this correlation in the ``nusselt`` field
of channel, fluidlink and thermalink components.

base.title: Built-in correlation to use as base
base.description:
Required only for Case 2: built-in correlation with custom parameters.
Identifies which built-in initialization to use for this entry.

NuL.title: Laminar Nusselt number (DBG only)
NuL.description: Minimum value applied in the DBG correlation: Nu = max(NuL, NuT).

nusselt_correlations.description:
Optional list of named Nusselt number correlations available to channel,
fluidlink and thermalink components. Three use cases are supported:
built-in with defaults, built-in with custom parameters, or user-defined
via external DLL. See :ref:`nusselt-correlations-details` for details and examples.

materials.title: Material database
materials.description:
Optional list of named materials available to ``strand``, ``solid``,
``solidlink``, and ``mesh2D`` components. Three use cases are supported:
built-in with defaults, built-in with custom parameters, or user-defined
via external DLL. See :ref:`materials-details` for details and examples.

Optional parameters: ``density``, ``RRR``, ``E0``, ``nPow``,
``Bc20m``, ``Tc0m``, ``nu``, ``Ca1``, ``Ca2``, ``e0a``, ``emax``,
``C0``, ``p``, ``q``, ``str1``, ``str2``,
``Bc20``, ``Tc0_p``, ``CC0``, ``n``.

components.title: List of components to describe the model

channel.title: channel
channel.description:
1D pipe filled with compressible helium

 .. code:: yaml   

   Example:
     - type: channel            # Component type
       id: pipe_3L_P1_Hol       # Component Id
       nodes: 193               # Number of nodes
       length: 147.66           # Total length of the pipe (m)
       diameter: 0.007          # Diameter of the pipe (m)
       initial: {p: 5.0e5, t: 4.3, u: 0}   # Initial conditions
       thermal: flux            # Heat transfer with a wall expected
       flux: 0                  # Zero flux in this specific case
       channel_link: yes        # Expected link with another channel component
       friction: blasius        # Friction factor correlation name

id.title: "id" has to be unique and it is used by the links components

nodes.title: Number of nodes equally distanced along the channel length - Only used in case of uniform mesh

oneOf.title: Total length (m) of helium channel - In case of uniform mesh
Length of each node (m) - In case of non-uniform mesh

diameter.title: Hydraulic diameter (m) - Constant value along the channel

area.title: Cross-section area (m^2) - Constant value along the channel
area.description:
To be used in case of Bundle Gap only - Otherwise,
the area is automatically calculated based on the diameter

thermal.title: Thermal boundary type of the channel
thermal.description:
Defining a wall temperature (``temp``), a thermal flux (``flux``) or specifying a link
(``link``) with another component are the options available to the user - Value if nothing
is specified by the user: ``flux``

temp.title: Wall temperature (K) - To be used if temp is assigned to thermal

flux.title: Thermal flux (W/m) - To be used if flux is assigned to thermal

channel_link.title: Hydraulic link with other channels - Mass, momentum and energy exchanges
channel_link.description: Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``false``

friction.title: Friction factor correlation name
friction.description:
Built-in names: ``blasius``, ``katheder``, ``central_spiral``.
Custom correlations can be defined in ``friction_correlations``
(see :ref:`top-level-configuration`).

nusselt.title: Nusselt number correlation name
nusselt.description:
Used only when ``thermal: temp``.
Built-in names: ``pipe``, ``DBG``.
Custom correlations can be defined in ``nusselt_correlations``
(see :ref:`top-level-configuration`).

strand.title: strand
strand.description:
1D composite strand that contains a superconducting material in parallel with a stabilizer
shunt

 .. code:: yaml   

   Example:
     - type: strand               # Component type    
       id: strand_3L_P1           # Component Id
       nodes: 193                 # Number of nodes
       length: 147.66             # Strand length        
       initial: {t: 4.3}          # Initial conditions
       CICC_inner_radius: 0.005   # CICC inner radius (m) for effective field 
                                  # computation - Useless in this specific case
       CICC_outer_radius: 0.0168  # CICC outer radius (m) for effective field
                                  # computation - Useless in this specific case
       stabilizer: 
         material: Copper         # Stabilizer name
         area: 308.66e-6          # Stabilizer cross-section area (m2)
       superconductor: 
         material: Nb3Sn_JAS      # Superconductor name
         area: 154.33e-6          # Superconductor cross-section area (m2)
       channel_link: yes          # Thermal contact expected with a channel component
       flux:                      # Thermal flux imposed from h5 data
         time:  {h5: Q_CS3L_1.h5, data: t} # Time (s) scenario
         x:     {h5: Q_CS3L_1.h5, data: x} # Space (m) scenario
         value: {h5: Q_CS3L_1.h5, data: d} # Flux in W/m (structure of the data
                                  # consistent with imposed time/space scenario)
         order:  1                # 1st order interpolation in time
         repeat: 0                # No scenario repeat
         event:  no               # No intervention on the time step management
       field: 0.0                 # No magnetic field (T)
       field_gradient: 0.0        # No magnetic field gradient (T/m)
       current: 0.0               # No current (A)

id.title: 'id' has to be unique and it is used for connections

nodes.title: Number of nodes equally distanced along the channel length - Only used in case of uniform mesh

oneOf.title: Total length (m) of helium channel - In case of uniform mesh
Length of each node (m) - In case of non-uniform mesh

material.title: Material name
material.description:
Built-in name for stabilizer: ``copper``
Custom materials can be defined in ``materials`` (see :ref:`top-level-configuration`).

material.title: Material name
material.description:
Built-in names for superconductor: ``nb3sn``, ``nbti``.
Custom materials can be defined in ``materials`` (see :ref:`top-level-configuration`).

flux.title: Heat load applied to strand component (W/m) - Can be a single value OR based on time interpolation OR time/space one

field.title: Magnetic field map (T) of the specific strand - Can be a single value OR based on time interpolation OR time/space one

field_gradient.title: Magnetic field gradient map (T/m) of the specific strand - Can be a single value OR based on time interpolation OR time/space one

current.title: Electric current (A) - Can be a single value OR based on time interpolation

solid.title: solid
solid.description:
The lumped mass approach is used to define the part of the structure in contact with CICCs -
A solid component is an array of solid chunks, each carrying its own temperature

 .. code:: yaml   

   Example:
     - type: solid                         # Component type
       id: chunk_3L_P1                     # Component Id
       length: [1.02,1.03, 1.03, 1.04]     # Length of each solid chunk along the
                                           # CICC trajectory
       volume: [1.48,1.49, 1.49, 1.50]     # Volume of each solid chunk
       initial: {t: 4.3}                   # Initial temperature
       material: stainless_steel           # Solid material
       channel_link: [yes, yes, yes, yes]  # Thermal link with a channel
                                       # component expected for each solid chunk
       solid_link: yes                 # Thermal link with other solid
                                       # components expected
       flux: 100.0                     # Uniform heat load of 100 W/m (optional)

id.title: 'id' has to be unique and it is used for connections

length.title: Length (m) of each metal chunk along the CICC trajectory

volume.title: Volume (m^3) of each metal chunk
volume.description:
A single scalar can be provided instead of a list: REIMS will fill the array with
that value repeated for every node.

conduction_between_nodes.title: Thermal conduction between metal chunks along the CICC trajectory

material.title: Material name
material.description:
Built-in names: ``copper``, ``nb3sn``, ``nbti``, ``stainless_steel``,
``glass_epoxy``, ``glass_kapton_glass``.
Custom materials can be defined in ``materials`` (see :ref:`top-level-configuration`).

channel_link.title: Thermal link with hydraulic channel per metal chunk

flux.title: External heat load (W/m) applied to solid component - Can be a single value OR based on time interpolation OR time/space one

mesh2D.title: mesh2D
mesh2D.description:
2D surface representing a slice of a 3D solid structure - Available for heat diffusion
treatment

.. note::

  **Gmsh mesh ordering requirements (current code limitation)**

  In the ``.geo`` file, all geometric entities (points, lines, surfaces) must be defined
  **before** any physical group. Among physical groups, **physical lines must appear before
  physical surfaces**. Failing to respect this order will cause element labels to be
  misassigned at runtime. This constraint is due to the current implementation of the mesh
  reader and may be removed in a future version.

.. code:: yaml   

  Example:
    - type: mesh2D                   # Component type
      id: slice00                    # Component Id
      mesh: meshing/sliceXY_00.msh   # Reference mesh file
      initial: {t: 4.3}              # Initial temperature imposed in all the geometry
      regions:                       # Introduces the list of labels that identify specific 2D
                                     # regions of the 2D geometry
        - label: SS                  # Label name
          material: stainless_steel  # Material name used in this specific region
          source:                    # Heat load scenario to be specified
            time:  {h5: Qcase_00.h5, data: t}  # Time scenario (s)
            value: {h5: Qcase_00.h5, data: d}  # Heat load scenario consistent with the
                                     # time array (W/m)
      edges:                         # Introduces the list of labels that identify specific 1D
                                     # boundaries of the 2D geometry
        - {label: BC_bound,   type: flux,  value: 0.0}  # No heat flux to the 1D boundary
                                     # identified by the label BC_bound
      channel_link:
        - OP_Sl00_Hole02             # label that is expected to be thermally connected
                                     # to a channel component
        - OP_Sl00_Hole01             # label that is expected to be thermally connected
                                     # to a channel component
      solid_link:
        - P00_Tur02_Sl00             # label that is expected to be thermally connected
                                     # to a solid component

id.title: 'id' has to be unique and it is used for connections

mesh.title: Mesh file specification with name and path defining the geometry location

extrusion_length.title: Extrusion length of the 2D slice (m)
extrusion_length.description: Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``1.062``

label.title: Name of the label that identifies a specific 2D region of the 2D geometry
label.description:
This label must exist in the .msh file generated by Gmsh software from a .geo file that
describes the 2D geometry and introduces such labels

material.title: Material name
material.description:
Built-in names: ``copper``, ``nb3sn``, ``nbti``, ``stainless_steel``,
``glass_epoxy``, ``glass_kapton_glass``.
Custom materials can be defined in ``materials`` (see :ref:`top-level-configuration`).

source.title: Heat load applied (W) to the region identified by the label

label.title: Name of the label that identifies a specific 1D boundary of the 2D geometry
label.description:
This label must exist in the .msh file generated by Gmsh software from a .geo file
that describes the 2D geometry and introduces such labels

type.title: The user can specify either a temperature or a thermal flux at the level of the considered 1D slice boundary

value.title: Imposed temperature (K) of thermal flux (W) depending on the type of the thermal boundary condition

channel_link.title: List of labels dedicated to thermal contact with hydraulic channel - If they exist

solid_link.title: List of labels dedicated to thermal contact with solid components - If they exist

junction.title: junction
junction.description:
A junction connects 1D helium channels together

.. code:: yaml   

  Example:      
    - type: junction  # Component type
      link:           # Several branches expected - In this specific configuration,
                      # outlet of pipe1 is connected to inlets of both pipe2 and pipe3
      - id: pipe1     # Channel id
        node: out     # Involved channel boundary
        kappa: 1      # Kappa=1 means no pressure loss increase at the junction
      - id: pipe2
        node: in
        angle:  90    # Angle between the reference pipe1 and the present branch
      - {id: pipe3,   node: in,   angle:  90}

link.description: A junction can link several branches together (not limited number)

id.title: Identification of one of the branches involved in the junction -
id.description: 'id' of the corresponding channel component is required

node.title: Specification of the channel boundary connected to the junction
node.description: It can be ``in`` for inlet or ``out`` for outlet

kappa.title: Correction of the pressure loss coefficient via the introduction of the factor ''kappa''
kappa.description:
Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``1.0`` (no pressure loss increase)

If ''kappa'' is specified by the user, it must only be defined on the first item (the 1st
branch is automatically referred as the reference one for this specific junction)

angle.title: Angle (degrees) between the reference branch (1st item) and the branch associated to the current item
angle.description:
Only define it from the second item

Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``0.0`` degree

fluidlink.title: fluidlink
fluidlink.description:
Fluid-FLuid link that connects one helium channel to another - Transverse mass, momentum and
energy exchanges are allowed

 .. code:: yaml   

   Example:      
     - type: fluidlink                  # Component type
       wetted_perim_channels: 31.42e-3  # Wetted perimeter delimiting the boundary
                                        # between the channels (m)
       link:  # Two channels must be identified - In this specific configuration,  
              # the cells 1 to 5 from pipeTF_Pan1_BG are connected to cells 1 to 5 
              # from pipeTF_Pan1_Hol
       - id: pipeTF_Pan1_BG    # Channel Id
         node: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] # Channel involved nodes
       - {id: pipeTF_Pan1_Hol, node: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]}  # Id + involved nodes are
                                                       # specified for this channel

wetted_perim_channels.title: Wetted perimeter delimiting the boundary between the channels (m)

nusselt.title: Nusselt number correlation name
nusselt.description:
Built-in names: ``pipe``, ``DBG``.
Custom correlations can be defined in ``nusselt_correlations``
(see :ref:`top-level-configuration`).

id.title: Identification of one of the channels involved
id.description: 'id' of the corresponding channel component is required

node.title: List of cell indexes that are connected to cells of the other channel component
node.description:
The lists of the two items must be the same size - The i-th element of the
item 1 list will be connected to the i-th element of the item 2 list

thermalink.title: thermalink
thermalink.description:
Fluid-Solid link that thermally connects one helium channel to one of the following components
(strand, solid or mesh2D)

.. code:: yaml   

  Example:
    - type: thermalink              # Component type
        contact_surface: [0.067, 0.067, 0.067, 0.067, 0.068, 0.068]  # Contact surfaces
                                    # in (m2) for each of the 6 contacts
        link:                       # One channel and one solid component are specified
                                    # in this specific configuration
        - id: pipeTF_Pan1_BG        # Id + involved nodes are specified for this channel
          node: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]  
        - id: MC_TF_Pan1_C          # Id + involved nodes are specified for this solid
          node: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
          distance: [0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01] # distances per chunk
                                    # used for the computation of the temperature
                                    # gradient within the considered chunk

wetted_perimeter.title: Wetted perimeter of the channel in contact with the strand (m)
wetted_perimeter.description: Link channel/strand only - Required for this specific configuration

contact_surface.title: List of contact surfaces (m2)
contact_surface.description:
Link channel/solid only - Required for this specific configuration - Each element represents
a contact between a given channel cell and its associated solid chunk.
A single scalar can be provided instead of a list: REIMS will fill the array with
that value repeated for every node.

heat_coefficient.title: Imposed heat transfer coefficient (W/m2/K)
heat_coefficient.description: Link channel/mesh2D only - Required for this specific configuration

nusselt.title: Nusselt number correlation name
nusselt.description:
Required for channel/strand and channel/solid configurations.
Built-in names: ``pipe``, ``DBG``.
Custom correlations can be defined in ``nusselt_correlations``
(see :ref:`top-level-configuration`).

link.description:
One channel and one of the following components (strand, solid or mesh2D) must be
identified - The channel component is always the first item

id.title: Identification of one of the components involved
id.description: 'id' of the corresponding component is required

node.title: List of cell indexes that are connected to cells of the other component
node.description:
To be used if the item corresponds to one of the following components (channel, strand or
solid) - The lists of the two items must be the same size - The i-th element of the item 1
list will be connected to the i-th element of the item 2 list

label.title: List of labels that are connected to cells of the channel component
label.description:
Must be used instead of ''node'' if the item corresponds to the mesh2D component.
The lists of the two items must be the same size - The i-th element of the item 1 (channel)
list will be connected to the i-th element of the item 2 (mesh2D) list

distance.title: List of distances (m) used for the computation of the temperature gradient within the solid chunks defining the solid component
distance.description:
Link channel/solid only - Required for this specific configuration - Property only defined
in the item dedicated to the solid component - Each element of the list represents the
distance involved in the computation of the temperature gradient within the associated
solid chunk - The list of distances and the list of nodes must be the same size.
A single scalar can be provided instead of a list: REIMS will fill the array with
that value repeated for every node.

solidlink.title: solidlink
solidlink.description:
Solid-Solid link that thermally connects a solid component with another, or a solid component
with a mesh2D slice.

 .. code:: yaml   

   Example:
     - type: solidlink         # Component type
       material: glass_epoxy   # Insulation material name
       thickness: [0.0]        # Zero thickness in this example,
                               # meaning that the current thermal contact is full
       link:
       - id: MC_TF_Pan4_R      # Id + involved node are specified for this solid
         node: [5]               
         distance: [2.430e-03] # distance used for the computation of the temperature gradient
                               # within the considered chunk
       - id: slice00
         label: [P00_Tur02_Sl00] # Id + label involved for this mesh2D component

contact_surface.title: List of contact surfaces (m2)
contact_surface.description:
Link solid/solid only - Required for this specific configuration - Each element represents
a contact between a given solid chunk and its associated one.
A single scalar can be provided instead of a list: REIMS will fill the array with
that value repeated for every node.

material.title: Insulation material name
material.description:
Name of the material used in case of thermal resistance consideration for this
specific Solid-Solid link.
Built-in names: ``glass_epoxy``, ``glass_kapton_glass``.
Custom materials can be defined in ``materials`` (see :ref:`top-level-configuration`).

thickness.title: List of insulation thicknesses (m)
thickness.description:
Each element represents a contact between a given solid chunk and its associated solid
chunk or label (in case of a mesh2D component) - A non-zero thickness of insulation for a
given contact is required in case of thermal resistance consideration -
Put 0.0 for a given contact if full thermal contact is expected.
A single scalar can be provided instead of a list: REIMS will fill the array with
that value repeated for every node.

link.description:
One solid component and one of the following components (solid or mesh2D) must be 
identified - The mesh2D component (if present) is always the second item

id.title: Identification of one of the components involved
id.description: 'id' of the corresponding component is required

node.title: List of solid chunk indexes that are connected to solid chunks or labels of the other component, depending on its type
node.description:
To be used if the item corresponds to a solid component - 
The lists of the two items must be the same size - The i-th element of the item 1 list will
be connected to the i-th element of the item 2 list

label.title: List of labels that are connected to solid chunks of the solid component
label.description:
Must be used instead of ''node'' if the item corresponds to the mesh2D component.
The lists of the two items must be the same size - The i-th element of the item 1 (solid)
list will be connected to the i-th element of the item 2 (mesh2D) list

distance.title: List of distances (m) used for the computation of the temperature gradient within the solid chunks defining the solid component
distance.description:
Property only defined for the item dedicated to a solid component - Each element of the
list represents the distance involved in the computation of the temperature gradient
within the associated solid chunk - The list of distances and the list of nodes must be
the same size.
A single scalar can be provided instead of a list: REIMS will fill the array with
that value repeated for every node.

pump.title: pump
pump.description:
A pump connects two 1D helium channels together

 .. code:: yaml   

   Example:    
     - type: pump    # Component type
       m0: 1e-3      # Mass flow rate: 1 g/s
       link:         # 2 links: link 1 - pump inlet, link 2 - pump outlet
        - id: pipe   # inlet of the pump connected to outlet of 'pipe'
          node: out  # outlet pipe
        - id: pipe   # outlet of the pump connected to inlet of 'pipe'
          node: in   # inlet pipe

link.description:
Two channels must be identified - The outlet of one channel component (1st link) must be
connected to the inlet of the other

compressor.title: compressor
compressor.description:
A compressor connects two 1D helium channels together

 .. code:: yaml   

   Example:    
     - type: compressor    # Component type
       m0:  0.002          # Mass flow rate parameter (kg/s)
       dp0: 3.3e5          # Pressure parameter (Pa)
       link:               # 2 links: link 1 - pump inlet, link 2 - pump outlet
        - id: pipe         # inlet of the pump connected to outlet of 'pipe'
          node: out        # outlet pipe
        - id: pipe         # outlet of the pump connected to inlet of 'pipe'
          node: in         # inlet pipe

m0.title: Mass flow rate parameter (kg/s) involved in the compressor characteristic definition

dp0.title: Pressure parameter (Pa) involved in the compressor characteristic definition

link.description:
Two channels must be identified - The outlet of one channel component (1st link) must be
connected to the inlet of the other

id.title: Identification of one of the branches connected to the circulator
id.description: 'id' of the corresponding channel component is required

node.title: Specification of the channel boundary connected to the circulator
node.description:
It can be ``in`` for inlet or ``out`` for outlet - However, the node of the 1st link must
be ``out``

boundary_PT.title: boundary_PT
boundary_PT.description:
Helium tank with imposed pressure and temperature acting as an inflow boundary condition - 
This inflow may become an outflow under certain circumstances

.. code:: yaml   

  Example:  
    - type: boundary_PT            # Component type
      p: 2.0e5                     # Tank pressure (Pa)
      t: 293.0                     # Tank temperature (K)
      link:  {id: pipe, node: in}  # Id + involved boundary are specified for this channel

id.title: Identification of the channel component for which the boundary condition is defined
id.description: 'id' of the corresponding channel component is required

node.title: Specification of the involved channel boundary
node.description: It can be ``in`` for inlet or ``out`` for outlet

hugoniot_boundary.title: Exact Rankine-Hugoniot relations at this boundary
hugoniot_boundary.description:
Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``no``

- ``yes``: Enforces conservation of mass, momentum and energy across the
  pressure wave at the boundary (exact Rankine-Hugoniot relations).
  Recommended for high-amplitude pressure transients (shocks, sudden
  pressure ramps).

- ``no``: Acoustic (linearized) approximation. Valid for low-amplitude
  pressure transients.

boundary_mT.title: boundary_mT
boundary_mT.description:
Helium inflow boundary condition with imposed mass flow rate and temperature

.. code:: yaml   

  Example:  
    - type: boundary_mT            # Component type
      mdot: 2.0e-3                 # Imposed mass flow rate (kg/s)
      t: 293.0                     # Imposed temperature (K)
      link:  {id: pipe, node: in}  # Id + involved boundary are specified for this channel

id.title: Identification of the channel component for which the boundary condition is defined
id.description: 'id' of the corresponding channel component is required

node.title: Specification of the involved channel boundary
node.description: It can be ``in`` for inlet or ``out`` for outlet

1D_signal.description:
.. code:: yaml

  Example:
    flux:                          # Heat load
      time:  [   0,  100]          # Time scenario (s)     - 2 instants
      x:     [ 0.0,  5.0,  10.0]   # Spatial positions (m) - 3 points
      value: [[0.1,  0.2],         # x=0.0m : value at t=0, t=100
              [0.3,  0.5],         # x=5.0m : value at t=0, t=100
              [0.2,  0.3]]         # x=10.0m: value at t=0, t=100
                                   # value dimension is [n_x=3 x n_time=2]
      order:  0                    # 0 order in time
      repeat: 0                    # No scenario repeat
      event:  implicit             # 3 consecutive explicit steps are enforced each time the simulation
                                   # physical time reaches one of the values specified in 'time'

  Example (in case of an external DLL):
    flux:
      external: my_signal_func  # Function name exported by the DLL
      my_param: 1.0             # Any extra parameters passed to the DLL at init

external.title: Function name exported by a DLL
external.description:
When ``external`` is present (the DLL must be declared in ``external_libs``),
``time``, ``x`` and ``value`` are not required.
The additional parameters defined in the same block as ``external`` are passed to the DLL
at startup. See the `DLL developer guide <../../../dll/_build/html/index.html>`_ for the required interface.

order.title: Time interpolation order (0 or 1)
order.description: Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``0``

repeat.title: Index from which the signal will be repeated
repeat.description: Value if nothing is specified by the user: ``0``

event.title: Event consideration based on Time data.
event.description:
It can be

    - ``'no'`` (value if nothing is specified by the user) if the user does not want to
      take care of specific events based on the 'time' data (the time step automatically
      evolves without intervention),
    - ``'explicit'``: 3 consecutive explicit steps are enforced each time the simulation
      physical time reaches one of the values specified in 'time',
    - ``'implicit'``: 1 implicit step is enforced each time the simulation physical time
      reaches one of the values specified in 'time'.

0D_signal.description:
.. code:: yaml

  Example:
    p:                          # Pressure
      time:   [     0,	   100] # Time scenario (s)
      value:  [500000,	600000] # Value (Pa)
      order:  1                 # 1st order in time activated
      repeat: 0                 # No scenario repeat
      event:  no                # No intervention on the time step management

  Example (in case of an external DLL):
    p:
      external: my_signal_func  # Function name exported by the DLL
      my_param: 1.0             # Any extra parameters passed to the DLL at init
